DNA solutions are a very rich and interesting system with a variety of phase transitions and a complex phase diagram.
, at least in the case of monovalent salts, the cholesterics are a stable thermodynamic phase in the whole range of DNA densities and temperatures, with the only exception of the condensed phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cholesterics are not a special case of liquid crystals.

the cholesterics are not the most stable phase of DNA solutions in monovalent salts at low temperatures, and the line hexatics are not the most dense phase of DNA solutions at high temperatures, in contrast to what is often believed in the literature.

DNA solutions in monovalent salts have two distinct regimes of phase transition: the cholesterically ordered regime and the isotropically ordered regime, and the transition between them is continuous.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the phase diagram for DNA solutions can be described by a single, universal equation of state that is independent of the nature of the salt.
the DNA phase diagram is a complex interplay of the electrostatic and the excluded volume interactions.
the line hexatic phase is not only a theoretical phase, but can be realized in practice.
